Interface Sweepable

All Known Subinterfaces:
AtomSpi, JournalSpi, MailboxSpi
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractAtomSpi, AbstractJournalSpi, AbstractMailboxSpi, CassandraAtomSpi, CassandraJournalSpi, DynamoDbAtomSpi, DynamoDbJournalSpi, DynamoDbMailboxSpi, EtcdAtomSpi, HazelcastAtomSpi, HazelcastJournalSpi, HazelcastMailboxSpi, InMemoryAtomSpi, InMemoryJournalSpi, InMemoryMailboxSpi, MongoDbAtomSpi, MongoDbJournalSpi, MongoDbMailboxSpi, NatsAtomSpi, NatsJournalSpi, NatsMailboxSpi, PostgresAtomSpi, PostgresJournalSpi, PostgresMailboxSpi, RabbitMqJournalSpi, RedisAtomSpi, RedisJournalSpi, RedisMailboxSpi
public interface Sweepable
A backend capability: can physically remove expired records on demand. Implemented by SPI interfaces for primitives that carry expirable state (AtomSpi, JournalSpi, MailboxSpi).

The Sweeper driver class calls sweep(int) on a scheduled cadence and uses the returned count to decide whether to keep draining in this tick or wait until the next scheduled call.

Backends with native TTL (Redis EXPIRE, DynamoDB TTL, Mongo TTL indexes, etc.) inherit a no-op default from their corresponding AbstractXSpi base class and need not override this method. Backends without native TTL (e.g., PostgreSQL) must override with a batched conditional delete — see the SPI javadoc on the specific primitive's interface for the full contract.

  • Method Details

    • sweep

      int sweep(int maxToSweep)
      Delete up to maxToSweep expired records from the backend.

      Return exactly 0 if nothing was found, exactly maxToSweep if the caller should drain again immediately, or something in between if there is no more work for this tick.

      Must be safe to call concurrently from multiple processes in a clustered deployment. For database backends, use the canonical "concurrent workers" pattern for your engine (e.g., SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on Postgres).

      Parameters:
      maxToSweep - maximum number of records to delete in this call; must be positive
      Returns:
      the actual number of records deleted
